lastText: ☰⚙Command TerminatedRecalled to MoscowMinor DefeatSoviet High Command, 1939–1945End of hostilities: OCTOBER 1941 (RECALLED) · filed late, out of sequenceImmediate AftermathThis campaign ends here, and not on the battlefield. Under NKVD Mode, suspicion tracked every choice that read as independence ██████ than obedience, and it has run out. The political apparatus, not the enemy, has judged this command a problem the █████ didn't have. What happens next covers a wider range than the usual telling admits. Most officers recalled under circumstances like █████ in 1941 were shot or sent to the camps, often within weeks and without a trial worth the name. A minority (Rokossovsky is the documented case, arrested in 1937 and released in 1940 once the war made his competence too valuable to █████) were eventually ██████████, sometimes years later, sometimes at the front they'd been pulled from. Which of the two this recall turns out to be is not knowable from inside it, and the odds do not favor the second. The war continues without you. It was never yours to ██████.One Year LaterThe war this command was ██████ from ends in Berlin regardless, under whoever answered for it after. A year past the recall, the file this campaign opened with (reinstated at the front, or █████ reinstated at all) has almost certainly already resolved one way or the other; the war itself did not wait to find out which.The Theater Map at the end of the warThe map at the end of 1941StartOCTOBER 1941: The war en
